source: Bank for International Settlements, debt securities statistics: total debt securities issued by residents of each economy, all issuer sectors, nominal value, US dollars, quarterly; the issuer split into governments, financial firms and non-financial companies from the same tables.
note: Each line is everything in bonds, notes and bills that the residents of one economy owe, at face value, so adding the lines gives the world's debt securities without counting an issuer twice across lines. The euro area is shown country by country and its aggregate is left out, since the aggregate already contains its members; the check under the chart states both figures. The three lines below the economies say how much of the total is owed by governments, by banks and other financial firms, and by companies. Figures are face value, as the BIS publishes them, while the ownership books on this tab carry bonds at market value, so the same country can read differently in the two places and the gap is a matter of valuation, not of coverage. A figure is carried forward for up to a year while the next release is awaited, and an economy whose newest figure is older than that drops out rather than repeating a stale number. Technical detail: BIS series by residence of issuer, sector S1 for the total and S13, S12 and S11 for the issuer split, in US dollars as published, no conversion applied.
